# Exercise 1

Without running the code, determine the result (or error) of each expression.

## R

```{r}
x = c(a = 2, b = 4, c = 6, d = 8)

x[c(1, 3)]          # Select positions 1 and 3
x[-c(1, 3)]         # Exclude positions 1 and 3
x[c(TRUE, FALSE)]   # Recycle the logical index; keep positions 1 and 3
x[c("d", "b", "z")] # Select by name; "z" produces NA
x[x > 3 & x < 8]    # Keep values strictly between 3 and 8
```

## Python / NumPy

```{python}
#| eval: false
x = np.array([2, 4, 6, 8])

x[[0, 2]]                    # Select positions 0 and 2
x[-2:]                       # Select the final two values
x[np.array([True, False])]   # Error: Boolean indexes do not recycle
x[x > 3 & x < 8]             # Error: incorrect operator precedence
x[(x > 3) & (x < 8)]         # Parenthesize each comparison
```

# Exercise 2

NumPy compares shapes from right to left. At each position, dimensions are compatible if they are equal or one of them is 1.

## Broadcasting shapes

```text
  (128, 128, 3)
            (3,)
  -------------
  (128, 128, 3)  # Succeeds: (3,) expands over the leading dimensions

  (8, 1, 6, 1)
     (7, 1, 5)
  -------------
  (8, 7, 6, 5)  # Succeeds: each pair matches or includes a 1

     (2, 1)
  (8, 4, 3)
  ---------
  incompatible  # Fails: 2 and 4 are incompatible

     (3, 1)
  (15, 3, 5)
  ----------
  (15, 3, 5)  # Succeeds: 1 expands to 5 and 3 matches 3

  (3,)
  (4,)
  ----
  incompatible  # Fails: 3 and 4 are incompatible
```

## Centering each row

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(523)
x = rng.normal(size=(100, 5))

centered = x - x.mean(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]  # Add a singleton dimension
centered.shape
centered.mean(axis=1)[:10]

centered = x - x.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)  # Preserve the reduced dimension
centered.shape
```
